subject: POC trial planning: workload & traffic profile intake - AcmeHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning: workload & traffic profile intake - AcmeHealth

Hi Sarah 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scheduled and scoped: 

What we heard (high level)
- Goal: validate LLM-driven triage + summarization for clinical intake forms (reduce triage time, improve routing).
- Success criteria you mentioned: p95 latency <= 200ms for 95% of live traffic during normal load, and classification/summary accuracy >= 92% based on your evaluation dataset.

To scope infrastructure and confirm timing, can you send a short traffic/workload profile (or confirm items below)? Ben will use this to size the Dedicated pool for the trial and validate cost estimates. Ideally we get this by EOD Monday so we can lock resources for the week of May 15.

Requested fields (simple table is fine):
- Baseline RPS (average sustained requests per second)
- Peak RPS and typical burst duration (e.g., 50 RPS bursts for 2–3 minutes)
- Token lengths (avg input tokens / avg output tokens) and top percentiles (p95 token length)
- Typical concurrency (number of simultaneous sessions)
- Expected daily volume (requests/day)
- Any rate-limiting or SLAs we should be aware of
- Representative sample file (CSV) if available  traffic_sample.csv works great

Proposed POC plan (we can iterate):
- Pre-POC: intake + quick run of sample traffic to validate tokenization and latency assumptions (1–2 days)
- POC trial: 2-week window with metrics collection (throughput, latency, cost, quality)
- Evaluation: we'll run your golden set and provide an evaluation report with recommendations and a rollback/next-steps plan

Ownership:
- Redwood SE: Ben Carter (technical setup, test harness, performance tuning)
- Redwood AE / CSM: me (Marissa Cole)  scheduling, success criteria alignment, procurement coordination
- AcmeHealth: Sarah Hayes (POC owner), please include procurement contact if we need contract/PO coordination

Attachments: we typically use a short test-plan template. Ben will send the filled version once we have your traffic sample.

Next steps:
1) Sarah: please send the workload profile + traffic_sample.csv and confirm target POC week (you suggested week of May 15).
2) Ben: will prepare a lightweight test plan + estimated Dedicated capacity and cost for the trial.
3) I will send a kickoff invite for a 30–45m technical kickoff (propose May 11) to align on access, sample ingestion, and evaluation metrics.

Thanks  look forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks, Marissa  great recap. Confirming details below and attaching traffic_sample.csv (sanitized).

Workload profile (current prod-ish traffic patterns):
- Baseline RPS (sustained): 5 rps (weekday business hours)
- Peak RPS (sustained for short windows): 50 rps (bursts up to ~2–4 minutes during morning rollout)
- Concurrency: typically 8–12 concurrent sessions; spike concurrency up to 30 during peak events
- Avg token lengths: input ~110 tokens (median 95), output ~320 tokens (median 300)
- p95 token length (input): 220 tokens; p95 output: 540 tokens
- Expected daily volume during trial: ~40k requests/day (we expect ramp from 5k/day to 40k/day during the trial as we shift traffic)
- SLA expectations: p95 latency <= 200–250ms (we are flexible on p95 given batching tradeoffs but want to understand cost/latency curves)

Success criteria (what we care about):
- Functional: summarization accuracy and classification precision >= 92% on our golden set
- Performance: p95 latency <= 250ms for baseline traffic; acceptable degradation during 2–4 minute bursts (we'll like a proposal for graceful degradation/fallback)
- Cost: total inference cost comparable to our current provider within 20% for the POC (we understand you'll provide an estimate)

Timing: week of May 15 works for the trial start. Before that we'll need a kickoff to discuss access and ingestion.

Attached: traffic_sample.csv (sanitized subset)  let me know if you need a larger sample. Procurement contact: procure@acmehealth.com (cc'd for later).

Thanks,
Sarah

AcmeHealth

Thanks for the sample, Sarah  this is very helpful. A few notes / clarifying Qs and the proposed technical plan: 

Quick clarifications:
- Token counts: I validated the sample. p95 numbers look correct (input ~220 / output ~540); that implies we should size for ~800 tokens per request to be conservative when calculating token throughput.
- Burst handling: For short 2–4 minute bursts to 50 RPS we recommend enabling dynamic burst capacity on Dedicated (short-lived nodes) + prefix caching where applicable.

Proposed test approach (technical):
1) Pre-POC (1–2 days): run the sanitized sample through our test harness to validate tokenization, warm KV cache, and get a latency baseline on a small Dedicated pool.
2) Baseline trial (week 1): route 10–20% of production traffic through Redwood to validate accuracy and latency under real traffic; collect metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, error rates).
3) Ramp (week 2): increase to the target traffic mix (up to the 40k requests/day target) to observe behavior under burst conditions. We'll run targeted stress pulses to validate fallback policies.
4) Evaluation: run your golden set and provide a report with suggested quantization/profile settings to meet your cost/latency targets.

Success criteria (technical):
- Performance: p95 <= 250ms at baseline sustained 5 RPS; during burst we aim to keep p95 <= 500ms and avoid error rate increase >0.5%
- Quality: model meets the >=92% accuracy threshold on the golden set
- Stability: no capacity-related 5xxs during 50 RPS bursts in staged tests

Preliminary resource estimate (ballpark):
- Small Dedicated pool with 2 x A100-equivalent instances for baseline validation; add 1–2 burst nodes for short windows to handle 50 RPS bursts (we'll provide detailed token-hour estimates once we run the sample).

Attachments: I attached a short POC test-plan template (poc-test-plan.xlsx) and our POC pricing summary (redwood-poc-pricing.pdf) to make procurement easier.

Ownership:
- SE lead: Ben Carter (will run harness + tuning)
- AE/CSM: Marissa (scheduling + success criteria)
- AcmeHealth: Sarah (data + golden set + procurement)

Next steps:
- Marissa: set kickoff meeting (proposed May 11)
- Sarah: confirm kickoff time and whether we should include a network/IT contact for ingestion and auth setup
- I'll run the sample Monday morning and send a short baseline report by EOD Monday.

Thanks  I'll follow up with the baseline numbers.

Ben
